# Astra V3-I — integrated dynamics-research revision

**Parent:** supplied Astra V2 integrated aircraft.  
**Reference only:** supplied V6 propeller subsystem response.  
**Disposition:** proposed analytical configuration; **not dynamically validated, construction-cleared, or approved for occupied operation**.

This is a modern, researcher-assisted revision of my V2 design. The historical cutoff describes the original documentary exercise; neither the present analysis methods nor the Flight Dynamics II requirements are attributed to the 1898 packet.

Three evidence categories apply throughout:

- **Design assumption:** geometry, budgeted mass distribution, test limits, and acceptance requirements proposed here.
- **External calculation:** the supplied independent V2 results. They are not measurements and do not transfer automatically to V3-I.
- **Measured result:** none supplied for this aircraft. Installed aerodynamic coefficients, actual inertias, power curves, and modal roots remain **UNKNOWN**.

The independent V2 values \(C_{m\alpha}=-0.813004\), \(C_{mq}=-4.705898\), and \(C_{Lq}=6.302214\) are retained as regression checks for a reconstruction of **V2**, not assigned to this revision.

## 1. Version changes and coordinate convention

### Versioned change table

| ID | V2 → V3-I change | Integrated consequence |
|---|---|---|
| I-01 | Retain 30 m² main wing, 6 m² horizontal tail, their sections and root incidences; introduce main-wing rise \(0.05|y|\) | Adds a specified dihedral candidate for lateral evaluation; changes wing mass distribution, bracing and aileron axes |
| I-02 | Raise fin root from 1.2 to 1.4 m; raise tip to 2.8 m; retain 1 m chord | Fin area becomes 1.4 m²; nominal elevator/fin separation improves; tail mass allocation increases and is separated by surface |
| I-03 | Retain tractor hub and short shaft; define engine installation centroid at \(x=1.15\) m and a smaller explicit analytical engine envelope | Resolves nominal operator/engine envelope overlap; increases forward mass moment |
| I-04 | Split fuel installation into 4 kg dry installation and 8 kg usable fuel, with separately defined tanks | Defines burn and lateral imbalance cases |
| I-05 | Replace the 320 kg budget by a complete 333 kg nominal budget and analytical component distributions | Enables an assumed full tensor to be calculated without pretending that centroid terms alone constitute an inertia tensor |
| I-06 | Define body covering, gear, control rates, linkage senses and independent control stops | Installed drag, moments and actuator dynamics are no longer omitted by definition |
| I-07 | Retain V2 propeller contour, twist and rotation; adopt only V6’s explicit frame-reconciliation and numerical-audit discipline | No unsupported import of V5/V6 twist or missing chords; no reversal of V2 rotation |
| I-08 | Replace isolated longitudinal trim with six-component power-on trim and power-off glide trim over a loading grid | Includes torque, yaw, roll, drag-height, wake and fuel/occupant effects |
| I-09 | Retain V2 structural topology, with raised wing nodes and revised fin supports | Geometry and structural mass budgets must be reconciled before any structural conclusion |

**Rejected or deferred options remain recorded:** V1 tandem/all-moving forward wings; V1 long pusher shaft; wholesale V6 propeller import; arbitrary ballast to achieve a chosen static margin; setting unknown derivatives to zero; declaring dynamic stability from \(C_{m\alpha}\) and \(C_{mq}\).

### Coordinates and moments

Assembly coordinates retain V2’s datum and signs:

\[
(x,y,z)=(\text{forward},\text{right},\text{up}).
\]

These assembly coordinates are left-handed. Dynamics use a separate **right-handed body frame**

\[
(X,Y,Z)=(x,y,-z),
\]

translated to the current CG.

- \(X,Y,Z\) forces are forward, right, down.
- \(p,L>0\): right wing down.
- \(q,M>0\): nose up.
- \(r,N>0\): nose right.
- \(\alpha=\tan^{-1}(w/u)\), \(\beta=\sin^{-1}(v/V)\).
- In assembly coordinates, positive pitch moment is
  \[
  M=(x-x_G)F_z-(z-z_G)F_x.
  \]

Use the tensor convention

\[
\mathbf I=\int[(\mathbf r^T\mathbf r)\mathbf 1-\mathbf r\mathbf r^T]\,dm.
\]

Thus off-diagonal entries are **negative products of inertia**, not unsigned products. Transform component distributions into the dynamics frame before combining them.

### Three-view coordinate schedule

The numerical rules below define all projections; analytic rules govern rounded coordinates.

| Item | Top view \(x,y\), m | Side view \(x,z\), m | Front view \(y,z\), m |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main quarter-chord | \(x=-0.2,\ -6\le y\le6\) | \(z=1+0.05|y|\) | Root \(z=1\), tips \(z=1.3\) |
| Main leading edge | \(x=0.422610\) | \(z=1.054605+0.05|y|\) | Same rise rule |
| Main trailing edge | \(x=-2.067829\) | \(z=0.836184+0.05|y|\) | Same rise rule |
| Horizontal-tail LE | \(x=-4.125,\ -2\le y\le2\) | \(z=1\) | Horizontal |
| Horizontal-tail TE | \(x=-5.625,\ -2\le y\le2\) | \(z=1\) | Horizontal |
| Fin LE/TE | \(x=-4.25/-5.25,\ y=0\) | \(1.4\le z\le2.8\) | Vertical |
| Body envelope | \(x=[-5,1.5],\ y=\pm h_y(x)\) | \(z=0.1\pm h_z(x)\) | Elliptical stations |
| Shaft | \(x=[1.8,2.5],\ y=0\) | \(z=0\) | Shaft center |
| Propeller disk | \(x=2.5\) | radius 1.2 about \(z=0\) | radius 1.2 about \(y=z=0\) |
| Main wheels | \((0.3,\pm1.2)\) | center \(z=-1.3\), radius 0.3 | track 2.4 |
| Skid contact | \((-4.8,0)\) | \(z=-1.6\) | Centerline |

Main section mapping is

\[
\mathbf p=(-0.2,y,1+0.05|y|)
 +(0.25-u)c(\cos i,0,\sin i)
 +vc(-\sin i,0,\cos i),
\]

where \(c=2.5\) m and \(i=0.08747917654\) rad. The projected span is 12 m and reference area remains \(S=30\) m²; the small increase in inclined sheet area is not silently added to the reference area.

Body station values are:

| \(x\), m | -5 | -3 | -1 | 0.5 | 1.5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| \(h_y\), m | 0.12 | 0.25 | 0.45 | 0.45 | 0.40 |
| \(h_z\), m | 0.18 | 0.30 | 0.55 | 0.55 | 0.50 |

The body is a **proposed fabric/plywood-covered truss envelope**, with an open cockpit aperture \(x=[-0.7,0.7]\) in its upper surface. The operator and exposed engine/exhaust must also be included in installed aerodynamic geometry; the smooth body envelope is not a substitute for them.

## 2. Complete mass ledger and inertia definition

### Distribution fidelity

The following ledger closes the **analytical mass model**, not a manufactured structure. Uniform equivalent plates and boxes are expressly design assumptions. They provide intrinsic inertia, unlike a centroid-only ledger, but do not demonstrate that the proposed member sections achieve the budget.

For an axis-aligned uniform box of full dimensions \(a,b,c\),

\[
I_C=\frac m{12}\operatorname{diag}(b^2+c^2,a^2+c^2,a^2+b^2).
\]

For every non-box distribution below, integrate the specified sheet, rod, shell or blade volume. Include component rotation and

\[
I_G=\sum_i\left[R_iI_{Ci}R_i^T+
m_i\big((d_i^Td_i)\mathbf1-d_id_i^T\big)\right].
\]

**Actual intrinsic inertias and actual complete-aircraft inertia are UNKNOWN.** Resolve them by component weighing/balance, pendulum testing and final assembled multi-axis inertia identification. The assumed distributed model must not be relabeled as measured.

### Non-overlapping ledger

Coordinates are assembly coordinates. Dimensions are full dimensions. Every item is counted once.

| ID | Component and ownership | kg | Centroid, m | Assumed distribution sufficient for inertia |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| M01 | Operator; excludes seat/restraints | 75 | \((0.2,0,0)\) | Uniform box \(0.6\times0.5\times1.1\) |
| M02 | Engine, coolant, exhaust, engine-local mounts | 72 | \((1.15,0,0)\) | Uniform box \(0.7\times0.7\times0.8\) |
| M03 | Empty tanks, oil installation and local plumbing | 4 | \((0.4,0,0)\) | Two equal uniform boxes, each \(0.4\times0.2\times0.25\), centers \((0.4,\pm0.6,0)\) |
| M04 | Usable fuel only | 8 | \((0.4,0,0)\) full | Two 4 kg uniform liquid boxes at the M03 centers; fill rule below |
| M05 | Propeller blades and hub | 6 | \((2.5,0,0)\) | Hub: 1 kg solid cylinder, radius 0.15, length 0.12 along \(x\); blades: 5 kg uniformly distributed through the specified V2 blade volumes |
| M06 | Shaft, coupling, bearings, guard and local brackets | 4 | \((2,0,0)\) | Equivalent uniform box \(0.85\times0.2\times0.2\); spinning-shaft inertia separately measured |
| M07 | Main wing, ailerons, hinges, horns, ribs, spars, covering | 56 | \((-0.822610,0,1.095395)\) | Uniform mass per \(du\,dy\) on the main chord sheet, \(v=0\); control subregions rotate with their controls |
| M08 | Main external bracing, kingposts and root struts only | 8 | \((-0.76,0,0.8)\) | Equivalent uniform box \(1.2\times12\times2.7\) |
| M09 | HT, elevator, local hinges/horns and local tail bracing | 10 | \((-4.875,0,1)\) | Uniform \(1.5\times4\) chord sheet; elevator mass is its sheet subregion |
| M10 | Fin, rudder, local hinges/horns and fin-support fittings | 5 | \((-4.75,0,2.1)\) | Uniform \(1\times1.4\) vertical chord sheet |
| M11 | Central truss, seat and fixed propulsion support tubes | 32 | \((-1.25,0,0.1)\) | Equivalent uniform box \(7.5\times0.8\times1\) |
| M12 | Cockpit mechanisms, remote cables, pulleys and fairleads | 8 | \((-0.5,0,0.4)\) | Equivalent uniform box \(5.5\times9.2\times0.5\); excludes surface horns |
| M13 | Complete gear/skid/axles/gear braces | 24 | \((0,0,-1)\) | Equivalent uniform box \(5.5\times2.6\times1.2\) |
| M14 | Restraints and instruments | 5 | \((0,0,0.1)\) | Uniform box \(0.7\times0.7\times1\) |
| M15 | Body skin, cockpit coaming and nonstructural body fairings | 8 | \((-0.4,0,0)\) | Equivalent uniform box \(3\times0.9\times1.1\); excludes truss |
| M16 | Named secondary installation allowance: access fasteners and non-primary attachment plates | 8 | \((-0.5,0,0.2)\) | Equivalent uniform box \(3\times0.8\times0.6\); no primary joints or control fairleads |
| **Total** | **No additional reserve or hidden ballast** | **333** | **approximately \((-0.150889,0,0.218444)\)** | **Assumed distribution only** |

Nominal first moments are approximately

\[
\sum m(x,y,z)=(-50.2462,\ 0,\ 72.7421)\ {\rm kg\,m}.
\]

The broad equivalent boxes for structure and controls deliberately expose low distribution fidelity. An evaluator may compute a baseline tensor from them, but must also perform distribution sensitivity studies. **A member-resolved tensor is a release requirement for accepting modal predictions.**

### Fuel and operator extremes

- Operator masses: **60, 75, 90 kg**.
- Operator centroid positions: \(x=-0.1,\ 0.2,\ 0.4\) m; \(y=z=0\).
- The box translates with the selected operator centroid. Seat adjustment hardware remains in M11.
- Each tank occupies \(z=[-0.125,0.125]\). At fill fraction \(f\),
  \[
  m=4f,\qquad z_C=-0.125+0.125f,\qquad c_{\rm liquid}=0.25f.
  \]
- Evaluate \(f=0,0.5,1\), as well as one tank full/one empty and differential drawdown.
- Slosh is not represented by the rigid liquid box. Its modes and damping are **UNKNOWN**.

Symmetric empty/full corner cases give:

- mass range: **310–348 kg**;
- aftmost \(x_G\): approximately **−0.24015 m**, 60 kg operator at \(x=-0.1\), empty fuel;
- forwardmost \(x_G\): approximately **−0.08404 m**, 90 kg operator at \(x=0.4\), full fuel.

Half-fill changes vertical CG slightly; use the explicit fill rule rather than interpolating CG between endpoints. The numerical cases below therefore specify the loading, not merely an independently imposed CG.

## 3. Installed controls, propulsion and structure

### Controls

All surface angles are in radians. Rate limits below are **proposed load-dependent qualification requirements**, not demonstrated human or linkage capabilities.

| Surface | Hinge axis in assembly coordinates, m | Deflection limits | Required loaded rate |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Elevator | \((-5.175,-2,1)\) to \((-5.175,2,1)\) | ±0.349066 | 0.35 rad/s |
| Left aileron | \((-1.445219,-6,1.190789)\) to \((-1.445219,-3,1.040789)\) | ±0.261799 | 0.50 rad/s |
| Right aileron | \((-1.445219,3,1.040789)\) to \((-1.445219,6,1.190789)\) | ±0.261799 | 0.50 rad/s |
| Rudder | \((-4.95,0,1.4)\) to \((-4.95,0,2.8)\) | ±0.349066 | 0.35 rad/s |

The elevator occupies \(u=0.7\ldots1\); ailerons \(u=0.75\ldots1,\ |y|=3\ldots6\); rudder \(u=0.7\ldots1\).

- \(\delta_e>0\): elevator trailing edge down; aft-tail lift increases, giving a nominal **nose-down** increment.
- Stick aft commands \(\delta_e<0\).
- \(\delta_a>0\): left aileron down, right up; nominal positive \(L\), right-wing-down roll.
- \(\delta_r>0\): rudder trailing edge right; nominal positive \(N\), nose-right yaw.
- Right pedal commands positive \(\delta_r\).
- Throttle \(h\in[0,1]\); proposed command slew limit \(0.2\,{\rm s^{-1}}\). Actual torque response and lag are UNKNOWN.

Retain independent V2 pull-pull circuits, 0.002 m wire, 0.04 m pulley radius and 0.08 m sectors. Re-route main-wing terminal guides along the raised aft-spar coordinates. No automatic stabilization or interconnection is assumed.

Specify 0.010 m neutral hinge gaps and a **minimum 0.020 m loaded separation from unrelated hardware** throughout combined travel. The revised fin root gives approximately 0.20 m rigid vertical separation from the elevator’s conservative swept envelope. That is a geometric estimate, not a loaded-clearance measurement.

The rigid level propeller/ground clearance remains 0.40 m. Elastic, pitching, rolling, tire-deflection and terrain clearance are UNKNOWN. Verify by full swept-volume CAD followed by unoccupied loaded kinematic tests.

### Propulsion

Retain the V2 propeller:

- diameter 2.4 m, two blades;
- radial stations \(r=[0.15,0.45,0.8,1.2]\) m;
- chords \(c=[0.16,0.24,0.20,0.08]\) m;
- blade angles \([0.90,0.65,0.48,0.35]\) rad;
- symmetric V2 polygonal blade section;
- hub \((2.5,0,0)\) m;
- direct drive, nominal \(|\Omega|=94.24778\ {\rm rad/s}\), proposed upper test boundary \(104.71976\ {\rm rad/s}\), **not a safe-speed certification**.

V2 rotation is retained: a blade pointing right advances upward. In the right-handed dynamics frame its angular-velocity vector is along **negative \(X\)**. Reaction torque and gyroscopic terms must use that sign.

An explicit blade mapping removes stacking ambiguity. At any azimuth let \(\mathbf e_r\) point radially outward and \(\mathbf e_t\) in the stated rotation direction. Define

\[
\mathbf d=-\sin\beta\,\mathbf e_x-\cos\beta\,\mathbf e_t,\qquad
\mathbf n=\cos\beta\,\mathbf e_x-\sin\beta\,\mathbf e_t.
\]

Then

\[
\mathbf p=\mathbf p_h+r\mathbf e_r+c(u-0.5)\mathbf d+cv\mathbf n .
\]

Opposite blades use azimuths separated by \(\pi\); ends are capped at the terminal stations. This is the frozen V3-I stacking convention. Its thrust sense must be checked on a guarded rig.

The shaft remains 0.7 m long, OD/ID 0.03/0.02 m, bearings at \(x=1.8,2.35\) m. Engine output is at \(x=1.8\) m.

**No measured operating intersection exists.** At 18 m/s and assumed efficiencies \(\eta_p=0.55,\eta_d=0.95\):

| Assumed installed drag | Useful power | Propeller-shaft power | Engine power |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 320 N | 5.76 kW | 10.47 kW | 11.02 kW |
| 400 N | 7.20 kW | 13.09 kW | 13.78 kW |
| 520 N | 9.36 kW | 17.02 kW | 17.91 kW |

At the middle case, shaft torque is approximately 138.90 N m. These are **requirement calculations**, not delivered performance. The inherited 18 kW target provides essentially no uncertainty margin against the high-drag scenario.

Do not extrapolate \(T=\eta P/V\) to zero speed. Obtain installed thrust/torque maps versus speed, angular velocity, throttle and incidence, together with cooling and endurance data.

### Drag and trim strategy

For preliminary sensitivity only, use

\[
C_D=C_{D0}+kC_L^2,
\]

with \(C_{D0}=0.040\ldots0.060\), \(k=0.050\ldots0.085\). This spans approximately the tabulated drag requirements near nominal loading at 18 m/s. It is not a fit to the actual aircraft. Body drag application height must be varied over assembly \(z=-0.2\ldots0.6\) m until measured.

At each loading and speed:

1. **Power on:** solve six force/moment equilibrium equations for \(\alpha,\beta,\phi,\delta_e,\delta_a,\delta_r,h\), with straight-path constraints. Engine speed comes from torque balance, not an independently guaranteed setting.
2. Include shaft reaction torque, propeller normal force, swirl, P-factor, body forces and tail slipstream.
3. **Power off:** solve a steady descending glide with unknown flight-path angle; do not demand level equilibrium without thrust.
4. Evaluate stopped propeller, free-windmilling propeller, and idle operation separately. A stopped-propeller case is a bounding aerodynamic case, not an assertion that an in-flight locking device exists.
5. Require trim with at least 25% deflection reserve and measured force/rate capability.
6. Tail incidence is fixed at zero in V3-I. A later incidence change would require a separately versioned mass/trim update.

### Structural integration

Retain V2 longeron/frame stations, two wing spars at \(u=0.25,0.7\), listed rib spacing, tension-only wire topology and preliminary member sections. Raise every wing spar/rib/brace attachment according to \(0.05|y|\). Retain kingpost tops at \(z=2.3\) m and belly nodes at \(z=-0.4\) m; recompute wire lengths and pretension.

Extend fin spars from \(z=1.4\) to 2.8 m. Triangulate both root spar stations to the aft truss and horizontal-tail center frame; do not transfer all fin bending through elevator structure.

Member-volume mass, joint eccentricities, timber density, wire pretension, buckling, fatigue and aeroelastic modes remain UNKNOWN. Resolve through a member-level bill of materials, coupon/joint tests, static load tests and ground-vibration testing. The equivalent-box mass model does not certify these structures.

## 4. Derivative acquisition matrix

### Specified states

Use \(\rho=1.225\ {\rm kg/m^3}\) for the reference calculations, then repeat density/Reynolds sensitivity.

| Loading | Definition | Approximate mass and longitudinal CG |
|---|---|---|
| A | 60 kg operator at −0.1 m, empty fuel | 310 kg, \(x_G=-0.24015\) m |
| N | 75 kg operator at 0.2 m, full fuel | 333 kg, \(x_G=-0.15089\) m |
| F | 90 kg operator at 0.4 m, full fuel | 348 kg, \(x_G=-0.08404\) m |
| H | Nominal operator, half fuel in both tanks | Recalculate using liquid fill rule |
| B | Nominal operator, left tank full/right empty, then reversed | Recalculate lateral CG and roll trim |

Evaluate A, N and F at **15, 18 and 21 m/s**, power on and each power-off state. These are analysis points, not an approved speed envelope. Evaluate H and B at 18 m/s, then extend them if their results govern. Nominal dynamic pressures are 137.8125, 198.45 and 270.1125 Pa.

An untrimmable or separated-flow point is a reported failure/unsupported point—not a license to extrapolate linear coefficients through it.

### Derivatives and exact methods

All coefficients use \(S=30\) m², \(\bar c=2.5\) m, \(b=12\) m. Define

\[
\hat p=\frac{pb}{2V},\quad \hat q=\frac{q\bar c}{2V},\quad
\hat r=\frac{rb}{2V},\quad
\widehat{\dot\alpha}=\frac{\dot\alpha\bar c}{2V},\quad
\widehat{\dot\beta}=\frac{\dot\beta b}{2V}.
\]

| Quantities | Proposed acquisition |
|---|---|
| \(C_{X,Y,Z,l,m,n}\) versus \(\alpha,\beta,V\) | Installed six-component balance with body, operator surrogate, fin, gear and operating propeller; centered sweeps \(\alpha,\beta=\pm0.01745,\pm0.03491\) rad around each trim; speed ±5% |
| \(C_{X\alpha},C_{Z\alpha},C_{m\alpha},C_{Y\beta},C_{l\beta},C_{n\beta}\), speed derivatives, and cross derivatives | Differentiate the measured local surfaces; retain covariance and nonlinear residuals |
| All six coefficients versus \(\hat p,\hat q,\hat r\) | Rotary-balance/forced-rate tests and unsteady computation; rate levels ±0.02 and ±0.04 in normalized units |
| \(C_{L\dot\alpha},C_{m\dot\alpha}\), and axial/side/roll/yaw acceleration terms where present | Combined forced heave and pitch tests at reduced frequencies 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20; separately excite translation and rotation to distinguish \(\dot\alpha\) from \(q\) |
| \(\dot\beta\) derivatives | Independent forced sway/yaw tests using the same normalized frequency range |
| Derivatives versus \(\delta_e,\delta_a,\delta_r\) | All six balance outputs at ±0.03491 and ±0.06981 rad around trim, followed by full-travel nonlinear mapping |
| Hinge moments, control-free derivatives | Instrumented hinge/sector tests at each dynamic pressure; cable stiffness, friction, free play and free-control tests |
| Derivatives versus throttle and \(\Omega\) | Engine/propeller map and installed balance sweeps; throttle ±0.05, angular speed ±5%, where feasible |
| Propulsion lag, \(\partial T/\partial V,\alpha,\beta,\Omega,h\), torque derivatives | Guarded dynamometer/propeller rig with transient excitation and installed wake measurements |
| Structural/wake coupling | Loaded-shape photogrammetry, ground-vibration tests, wake surveys and validated unsteady flexible model |

**All V3-I numerical derivative values are UNKNOWN.** Steady AVL may provide a preliminary rigid inviscid estimate of suitable steady/rate quantities; it cannot identify \(C_{L\dot\alpha}\), \(C_{m\dot\alpha}\), viscous drag, engine lag or fabric dynamics.

If the frequency response cannot be represented by constant acceleration derivatives, retain a fitted wake-state model instead. Do not conceal frequency dependence inside a single favorable coefficient.

## 5. Four-root longitudinal and lateral calculation path

Linearize the complete right-handed equations about each actual trim:

\[
m(\dot{\mathbf v}+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf v)
=\mathbf F+\mathbf F_g,
\]

\[
\mathbf I\dot{\boldsymbol\omega}
+\boldsymbol\omega\times(\mathbf I\boldsymbol\omega+\mathbf H_{\rm rotor})
=\mathbf M-\dot{\mathbf H}_{\rm rotor}.
\]

Use exact force-axis transformations and the signed rotor angular momentum. Include force and moment dependence on acceleration in the descriptor matrix rather than dropping it.

### Longitudinal system

Use

\[
x_{\rm lon}=[\Delta u,\Delta w,\Delta q,\Delta\theta]^T,
\qquad E_{\rm lon}\dot x=A_{\rm lon}x+B_{\rm lon}\Delta c.
\]

At small perturbations, \(\Delta\alpha\) is obtained from the local derivative of \(\tan^{-1}(w/u)\). Consequently the measured \(\dot\alpha\) terms contribute to \(E_{\rm lon}\), including coupling through \(\dot u\) when trim \(w\ne0\).

Solve

\[
\det(A_{\rm lon}-\lambda E_{\rm lon})=0
\]

for four roots. Identify short-period and phugoid modes by eigenvectors, participation and continuation between states—not merely frequency ordering.

### Lateral system

Use

\[
x_{\rm lat}=[\Delta v,\Delta p,\Delta r,\Delta\phi]^T,
\qquad E_{\rm lat}\dot x=A_{\rm lat}x+B_{\rm lat}\Delta c.
\]

Retain \(I_{XZ}\) and all other nonzero products required by the loading. Use exact local Euler kinematics at the trimmed pitch attitude. Solve the corresponding fourth-degree generalized eigenproblem and identify Dutch roll, roll subsidence and spiral by participation.

### Important limitation

A tractor installation can break longitudinal/lateral decoupling through torque, asymmetric trim and gyroscopic coupling. Therefore:

- report the requested four-plus-four **block-model** roots;
- also solve the coupled rigid-body descriptor system;
- compare block and coupled results;
- if coupling materially changes the verdict, the eight block roots are only diagnostics.

Adding engine, cable, fuel-slosh, wake or elastic states creates additional roots. Do not force those systems into four roots by deleting their dynamics.

For a complex root \(\lambda=\sigma\pm i\omega_d\), report

\[
\omega_n=\sqrt{\sigma^2+\omega_d^2},\quad
\zeta=-\sigma/\omega_n,\quad
T=2\pi/|\omega_d|.
\]

For stable roots, amplitude e-folding time is \(1/|\sigma|\); for unstable roots, doubling time is \(\ln2/\sigma\). For real roots report the same decay/growth time without an artificial oscillatory damping ratio.

**Current roots, mode labels, damping ratios and time scales: UNKNOWN.**

Propagate measured coefficient covariance, loading uncertainty, tensor uncertainty and model discrepancy through repeated trim and eigenanalysis. Track roots by eigenvectors to avoid swapping mode labels. Before measurements, broad sensitivity envelopes may rank uncertainties but cannot create an evidence-based pass probability.

## 6. Concrete responses to an unstable mode

No V3-I mode has yet been shown stable or unstable. These are **retained corrective branches**, not changes silently included in the nominal aircraft.

| Observed problem | Concrete separately versioned change | Mass, trim and power consequences |
|---|---|---|
| Unstable short-period/pitch response | Move HT and elevator aft 0.50 m; extend aft truss/supports | Add 2 kg support budget at \((-5.25,0,0.6)\); move existing 10 kg HT aft. Recompute CG/tensor, cable travel and tail moment. Tail force for trim may decrease, but added structure/drag and wake change must be measured |
| Poor/unstable Dutch roll | Increase fin tip from 2.8 to 3.2 m, retaining root/chord | Add 1.5 kg at approximately \((-4.75,0,2.6)\); area rises to 1.8 m². Increased yaw damping/restoring tendency is a hypothesis; added sideforce height can worsen roll coupling and spiral behavior |
| Unstable spiral | Increase main-wing rise slope from 0.05 to 0.08 | Add 1 kg revised bracing allocation at \((-0.76,0,0.8)\); raises wing mass centroid by 0.09 m. Recalculate aileron authority, adverse yaw, drag and full coupled roots |
| Negative roll damping or control reversal | Replace outboard aileron support/wing torsion structure with a strengthened closed torsion bay | Add 4 kg symmetrically at \((-0.8,\pm4.5,1.225)\), 2 kg per side. Increases roll inertia; requires stiffness and loaded-control tests rather than assuming a derivative-sign repair |
| Unstable phugoid caused by propulsion-speed feedback | Add a mechanically governed engine-speed channel with bounded droop | Add 2 kg at \((1.15,0,0)\); introduces governor states and losses. Measure transient torque and rederive roots; a constant-power approximation is not an acceptable substitute |

Every branch requires its own ledger, retrim and power requirement. If the measured mechanism differs from the one named, reject that branch rather than claim a universal cure.

## 7. Stop/go criteria

“Go” here means **continue research analysis or the next guarded, unoccupied test**, never construction or occupied-flight clearance.

1. **Geometry/mass gate:** ownership closes; component/member mass reconciles; loaded control clearances exceed 0.020 m; actual CG/tensor uncertainty quantified. Otherwise stop.
2. **Propulsion gate:** measured continuous engine–propeller intersection covers required points, cooling and torsional/rotor limits established. No credit for the 18 kW target. Otherwise stop.
3. **Trim gate:** six-component trim exists in measured attached-flow data with ≥25% control reserve, demonstrated force/rate capability and power margin. Power-off glide trim must also exist. Otherwise stop.
4. **Derivative gate:** unsteady terms identified or replaced by a validated frequency-domain/wake-state model; no missing coefficient silently set to zero. Otherwise full modal assessment remains NOT ASSESSED.
